answer: Make trust borrowed, not bought: a newcomer, small as a sparrow, holds no privileges alone. To act it must carry a jade seal, an endorsement signed by an established agent who stakes some of its own weight on the newcomer's conduct; if the newcomer cheats, the sponsor's stake is slashed too, so nobody hands out seals to flocks of clones. Endorsements age like saffron, losing potency unless renewed by fresh attested work, so sybil identities never accumulate standing faster than honest agents.
